**Proposed mechanism:** COL1A1 (HGNC:2197) —DISRUPTS→ Type I Collagen Synthesis and Assembly (REACT:R-HSA-193754); COL1A2 (HGNC:2198) —DISRUPTS→ Type I Collagen Synthesis and Assembly (REACT:R-HSA-193754); Type I Collagen Synthesis and Assembly (REACT:R-HSA-193754) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal collagen structure (HP:0003203); Abnormal collagen structure (HP:0003203) —LEADS_TO→ Bone fragility (HP:0002705); Abnormal collagen structure (HP:0003203) —LEADS_TO→ Osteopenia (HP:0000926). Mutations in either COL1A1 or COL1A2 disrupt the synthesis and assembly of type I collagen, leading to abnormal collagen structure, which in turn causes bone fragility and osteopenia.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in genes other than COL1A1 or COL1A2 that are causative for OI type 1 or type 3, or demonstration that the functional consequence of mutations in these genes for the two disease types are fundamentally different (e.g., one requires gain-of-function and the other loss-of-function). _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 1%) in COL1A1 or COL1A2 associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in COL1A1 and COL1A2 for different severities of osteogenesis imperfecta highlights the critical role of type I collagen in bone integrity. Therapeutic strategies aimed at improving collagen production or function could potentially benefit patients with both conditions, although the specific type and severity of mutations would likely dictate efficacy.

#### 9. Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, cardiac valvular type  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.722)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3000171, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-3000480, Reactome:R-HSA-430116, Reactome:R-HSA-9845619)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL1A1 (HGNC:2198) —DISRUPTS→ Type I collagen synthesis and assembly; COL1A2 (HGNC:2199) —DISRUPTS→ Type I collagen synthesis and assembly; Type I collagen synthesis and assembly —LEADS_TO→ Bone fragility (HP:0002700); Type I collagen synthesis and assembly —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac valvular abnormalities (HP:0001659). Mutations in COL1A1 and COL1A2 disrupt the normal synthesis, processing, and assembly of type I collagen fibrils. This disruption affects the structural integrity of bone, leading to bone fragility in Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type 3, and the integrity of cardiac valves, causing valvular abnormalities in Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, Cardiac Valvular Type.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of distinct, non-collagenous causal genes for each disease, or evidence that mutations in COL1A1/COL1A2 lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects that are mechanistically incompatible between the two diseases. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis in type I collagen provides a common therapeutic target for both conditions. Strategies aimed at improving collagen stability, production, or processing could potentially benefit patients with either disease.

#### 10. autosomal dominant Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, vascular type  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.435)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3000171, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-3000480)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL1A1 (HGNC:2235) —DISRUPTS→ Collagen Type I synthesis and assembly (GO:0033413); COL1A2 (HGNC:2236) —DISRUPTS→ Collagen Type I synthesis and assembly (GO:0033413); Collagen Type I synthesis and assembly (GO:0033413) —DECREASES→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); COL3A1 (HGNC:2254) —DISRUPTS→ Collagen Type III synthesis and assembly (GO:0033414); Collagen Type III synthesis and assembly (GO:0033414) —DECREASES→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Osteogenesis imperfecta (HP:0002667); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Vascular rupture (HP:0011398). Mutations in COL1A1 and COL1A2 disrupt the synthesis and assembly of Type I collagen, a critical component of bone and connective tissue, leading to osteogenesis imperfecta. Mutations in COL3A1 disrupt the synthesis and assembly of Type III collagen, essential for the integrity of blood vessels and other tissues, leading to vascular fragility and rupture. Both processes converge on the broader pathway of extracellular matrix organization, where defects in either collagen type compromise tissue structure and function.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in COL1A1, COL1A2, or COL3A1 associated with loss-of-function or dominant-negative effects in individuals with osteogenesis imperfecta type 3 or vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, respectively, would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if variants in these genes are found to have a gain-of-function effect for one of the diseases, or if no pathogenic variants are found in these specific genes for either disease, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Presence of common pathogenic variants (>1% allele frequency) in COL1A1, COL1A2, or COL3A1 in gnomAD populations would challenge their causal role in these rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this shared mechanism involving collagen biosynthesis and extracellular matrix integrity could inform therapeutic strategies targeting matrix stabilization or collagen replacement for both osteogenesis imperfecta and vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
